Fixed. `dayjs.tz()` only treated string input as a wall-clock time in the target zone; a `Date`, a numeric timestamp or a Day.js object was fed through the same wall-clock path, so the instant got shifted by the zone offset. Non-string input now goes through the normal conversion path (`d(input).tz(timezone)`), so the instant is kept and displayed in the target zone.

Verified: `dayjs.tz(new Date('2020-08-07T12:00-07:00'), 'America/Vancouver').format()` → `2020-08-07T12:00:00-07:00` (same for `.getTime()` and `dayjs(d)`); string input is unchanged.

Fixed. In `proto.tz` the offset difference was computed from `toDate()` (which carries milliseconds) against a wall-clock string that has second resolution, so a fractional second leaked into the offset as a fraction of a minute (e.g. 539.9957 → `+08:59`). The difference is now rounded to whole minutes.

Verified: `dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z')` → `+09:00`, and `.format()` → `2020-08-06T12:48:10+09:00`.

The difference is now rounded to whole minutes.

Verified: `dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z')` → `+09:00`, and `.format()` → `2020-08-06T12:48:10+09:00`.

Fixed. The `nl` locale's `ordinal` was a constant `${n}.`; it now picks the Dutch suffix by number: `ste` for 1, 8 and 20+, `de` otherwise. The result is wrapped in `[...]` (the same convention the `sv`/`en-gb` locales use) so the advancedFormat `Do`/`wo` tokens don't re-parse the suffix letters as format tokens.

Verified: 1 → `1ste`, 8 → `8ste`, 19 → `19de`, 20 → `20ste`, 2 → `2de`, and `dayjs('2018-05-08').locale('nl').format('dddd D MMMM YYYY')` → `dinsdag 8 mei 2018`.

import dayjs from '../src'
import utc from '../src/plugin/utc'
import timezone from '../src/plugin/timezone'
dayjs.extend(utc).extend(timezone)
it('edge cases', () => {
  const NY = 'America/New_York'
  // string wall-clock still works
  expect(dayjs.tz('2014-06-01 12:00', NY).format()).toBe('2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00')
  expect(dayjs.tz('2014-06-01 12:00', NY).utcOffset()).toBe(-240)
  // Date / number / dayjs object: instant preserved, shown in target zone
  expect(dayjs.tz(new Date(1401638400000), NY).format()).toBe('2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00')
  expect(dayjs.tz(1401638400000, NY).format()).toBe('2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00')
  expect(dayjs.tz(dayjs(1401638400000), NY).format()).toBe('2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00')
  expect(dayjs.tz(new Date(1401638400000), NY).valueOf()).toBe(1401638400000)
  expect(dayjs.tz(1401638400000, NY).valueOf()).toBe(1401638400000)
  // tz instance -> other zone
  expect(dayjs.tz('2014-06-01 12:00', NY).tz('Europe/London').format()).toBe('2014-06-01T17:00:00+01:00')
  expect(dayjs.tz(dayjs.tz('2014-06-01 12:00', NY), 'Europe/London').format()).toBe('2014-06-01T17:00:00+01:00')
  // utc instance
  expect(dayjs.utc('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz(NY).format()).toBe('2014-06-01T08:00:00-04:00')
  // no-arg
  expect(typeof dayjs.tz(undefined, NY).format()).toBe('string')
  expect(dayjs.tz.guess()).toBeTruthy()
})
EOF

arguments.text: Confirmed: `weekYear()` only handles the "week 1 in December" case, so a date in early January that still belongs to the previous week-year (week 52/53) is reported with the new year. I'm adding the January counterpart.

Confirmed: the customParseFormat `A` token only matches a literal `AM`/`PM`, so a locale meridiem such as zh-cn's `凌晨` never matches and the parse throws (→ Invalid Date). I'm making `A`/`a` use the locale's meridiem function.

Confirmed: the duration plugin's unit→milliseconds table has no `milliseconds` entry, so `dayjs.duration(1, 'ms')` multiplies by `undefined` (NaN) and ends up as an empty duration. Adding the missing unit.
